headline: Developmental disabilities program for WA families to be cut, but not ended
summary: Washington state maintains funding for the Parent to Parent program despite a 10% cut due to budget constraints. The program supports families of children with developmental disabilities and faced potential elimination earlier this year. State officials plan further spending reductions, likely targeting newer programs.

headline: OPINION: ‘Summery’ check in with voters
summary: A legislative candidate forum revealed Nebraskans' concerns about data centers and protecting the Environmental Trust Fund.

headline: Mystery price tag: Utah can’t say how much it’s losing from data center tax break
summary: Utah forgoes millions in revenue by exempting sales tax for data centers, yet lacks transparency on the extent of this loss. The state has no idea how much it's losing due to a repealed reporting requirement nearly two decades ago. This lack of data makes it difficult for policymakers to evaluate the tax exemption program and could impact budget decisions, as the potential revenue loss is significant enough to fund substantial benefits or cover large gaps in the state's Medicaid budget.

headline: ICE released man formerly detained in Aurora without his ID in unfamiliar state
summary: ICE detained Rudy Villeda Mejía for four months despite his pending T-visa application, intended for human trafficking victims. He was released and transferred between states without clear communication to his family or attorney. A judge ordered ICE not to detain him again unless he poses a flight risk or danger. The incident highlights challenges in locating detained immigrants and accessing legal services.

headline: Virginia voters to decide on 1% sales tax for school construction, NoVa transit funding
summary: In Virginia, voters across 47 jurisdictions will decide this fall whether to impose a 1% sales tax to fund school construction and modernization. The new funding tool, passed after years of legislative debate, aims to address aging schools and rising demand for transit support in Northern Virginia. About 58% of counties and cities aren't seeking the authority currently. Meanwhile, the Virginia Board of Education approved $577 million in grants for school construction projects across the state.

headline: ‘Springfield is under siege right now.’ ICE agents in Ohio have detained two Haitian pastors
summary: Following a Supreme Court ruling ending Temporary Protected Status for Haitians, ICE detained over 40 Haitians in Springfield, Ohio. Faith leaders criticized these detentions and called for an end to deportations tearing families apart. Haitians face fears of leaving home due to ankle monitors, with many reporting inhumane treatment. Advocates demand an end to ankle monitor use and criticize the government's self-deportation incentives as putting Haitians at risk upon return.

headline: Brother of migrant shot by ICE agent in Houston released from detention
summary: The Houston Police Department's Immigration Agent shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo on Canal Street, sparking a memorial at the site.

headline: Federal government allows return of U.S. citizen deported after traffic stop in Central Texas
summary: A Texas resident, Brian José Morales Garcia, was deported to Mexico despite having a birth certificate showing he was born in Denver. This raises questions about immigration enforcement and potential misinterpretation of legal status.

headline: Schools in Barre start the year without a district budget
summary: Vermonters struggle to pass school budgets; Barre Unified Union School District began year without approved budget due to differing tax impacts on city and town residents. Lack of budget forces district to take out line of credit, incurring monthly interest payments up to $22,000.
